items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: Benji White, he carried the sax section. While Pinky didn't read too well, he was a mediocre reader as far as musicianship was going. But he standing up there in the front with a baton, but he couldn't handle his shoulder.

ctx.x: and it's the 10th of November, 1986. Who were the leaders and managers of the Owls through the years?

Earl Crum was the manager. Leader? I don't think there was any leader. They just put the music out there on the stand and they went along and if they did any improvising they did it as a group to go along there, but they didn't read too well. You agree with me, Godfrey? Yeah. Sieg Christensen, when he joined the band, he read fairly well and Dan LeBlanc read fairly well. He was the tuba player and Bill read a little bit, trumpet player and Pinky didn't read that well, but Benji White, he carried the sax section.…
And then after Crum left, what happened? How did that happen? Well, after Crum left,

items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: I used to see Benji occasionally.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, Benji. I used to see Benji occasionally.
